page: Microsoft Azure D16alds_v6 is a low-memory variant of the general-purpose Daldv6 family, powered by AMD EPYC 9V74 processors. It provides 16 vCPUs across 8 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled, clocked at 3.7 GHz. The system includes 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. For high-speed temporary storage, it bundles 944 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. The processor architecture is x86_64 and features instruction set extensions including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 support), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-thread execution, driven by high clock speeds and modern Zen core architecture. In synthetic tests, stress-ng single-core performance and Geekbench single-core scores rank in the top 25 percentile, accompanied by strong results in Geekbench text processing and small-model LLM text generation. Multi-threaded performance across stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark tests falls within the middle 50 percentile. Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth measures lower at 36.92 GB/sec, placing in the bottom 25 percentile, while cached memory access registers 1216.65 GB/sec.

The 1:2 memory ratio presents an intentional tradeoff, catering to compute-heavy tasks that do not demand substantial memory capacity per thread. The integrated 944 GB local NVMe disk provides direct low-latency I/O for temporary staging, caching, or swap space, avoiding reliance on network-attached storage for ephemeral data. Consequently, resource density is skewed toward CPU cycles rather than large in-memory working sets.

The D16alds_v6 fits workloads requiring strong per-core CPU capability alongside modest memory footprints. Key applications include continuous integration build agents, code compilation, web application servers, containerized microservices, batch processing, and caching layers with local disk dependencies.
description: Microsoft Azure D16alds_v6 is a compute-focused instance from the general-purpose Daldv6 series. It features 16 vCPUs across 8 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. Accompanied by 32.0 GB of RAM, the instance maintains a reduced 2.0 GB per core ratio while offering 944 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 architecture incorporates advanced vector instructions including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16. Benchmarks highlight strong single-core CPU throughput, reaching top-tier ratings in stress-ng and Geekbench tests, alongside average multi-core and database performance. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth is comparatively constrained. Balancing solid single-thread performance with local NVMe caching, the D16alds_v6 is suited for CI/CD compilation pipelines, web serving, microservices, and compute-heavy batch processing jobs that do not demand extensive RAM.
